purpose: Activate an action, with intent independent of emphasis.
invariants: Use a native action element. Navigation belongs to Link.
Loading prevents duplicate activation and preserves the accessible name.
Keyboard focus remains visible in both modes.

component: native action semantics and safe default type
host: event handling, async operation state and native form intent

requirements.statement: Render a native button with default type=button; forward native button attributes and event handlers while owning disabled/loading semantics and visual data attributes.
Choose type=submit explicitly when submitting a form. Use Link for navigation and keep action authorization/business effects in the caller.

Set native disabled when disabled or loading is true and expose aria-busy while loading. Preserve the label DOM; without a leading icon hide label/trailing-icon paint by opacity and center a spinner, otherwise replace the leading icon with the spinner.
Supply meaningful text or aria-label/aria-labelledby, including for icon-only use. Loading preserves existing label content but cannot create a useful name from unnamed children.
Represent intent, emphasis and size independently with data attributes; default to default intent, primary emphasis and medium size without changing native interaction behavior.

Native disabled/loading prevents activation. aria-disabled alone supplies styling/semantics but the plain native Button does not suppress its handlers; a composing primitive or host must implement that behavior.
Use an instance-specific gradient identifier for nonprimary AI icon foregrounds and a hidden SVG definition; clone supplied React icon elements only to apply the intended stroke style.
Retain trigger-group keyboard focus indication in both modes and forced-color treatment. Use group tokens for state geometry and palette, and verify actual focus/contrast in the rendered context.

limitations: The component does not await onClick, own pending state or prevent duplicate requests before the host sets loading.
Disabled native controls may lose focus; no explicit focus recovery, confirmation or authorization policy is supplied.
